profile.summary: AlphaFold 2 predicts the three-dimensional structure of a protein from its amino acid sequence. It first searches sequence databases to build a multiple sequence alignment and find structural templates, then runs a neural network that reasons jointly over the alignment and over pairs of residues, and finally outputs atomic coordinates with a per-residue confidence score. This repository is the inference pipeline, and it also includes AlphaFold-Multimer for predicting complexes of several chains.

sections.title: How it works
sections.body: The pipeline has two halves. First, standard search tools, which the paper names as jackhmmer and HHBlits, build a multiple sequence alignment from the sequence databases, and templates are taken from homologous structures where available. Then the network runs: a trunk of 48 Evoformer blocks that passes information between the alignment representation and a pairwise representation of residue relationships, followed by a structure module that gives each residue an explicit rotation and translation and so places the atoms. The whole network is applied several times over, feeding its own output back in, which the authors call recycling. A relaxation step with Amber then fixes local geometry, and the five models are ranked by predicted LDDT.

sections.title: Versions and reproducibility
sections.body: A result must name three things: the code version, the parameter set and the databases. The presets are monomer, monomer_casp14, monomer_ptm and multimer. The parameter sets are dated tar files, and the README explains how to go back to the 2022-03-02 (v2.2.0) or 2022-01-19 (v2.1.0) multimer weights. The v2.3.0 technical note says the current multimer weights were fine-tuned with a new training cutoff of 2021-09-30, keeping the same model architecture. The databases that the download scripts fetch are not the CASP14 versions, and the README lists the exact CASP14 database releases for anyone reproducing that work. Some targets have high run-to-run variance over random seeds. The authors call AlphaFold-Multimer a work in progress that is not expected to be as stable as the monomer system, and it also needs the UniProt database.

sections.title: What it costs to run
sections.body: The README is specific about the setup. Linux only, up to 3 TB of disk for the databases (556 GB to download, 2.62 TB unpacked) and an NVIDIA GPU; larger proteins need more GPU memory. The reduced_dbs preset asks for 8 CPU cores, 8 GB of RAM and 600 GB of disk. The reference machine was 12 vCPUs, 85 GB of RAM and one A100. Prediction alone, excluding the database searches, took 4.9 s for 100 residues and 18,824 s for 5,000 residues on one A100.

facts.value: PDB structures. Versions before v2.3.0 were trained on structures released before 2018-04-30; the v2.3.0 AlphaFold-Multimer weights use a cutoff of 2021-09-30, about 30% more data, with training crops raised from 384 to 640 residues and a self-distillation set built from clustered MGnify.

facts.label: Known versions
facts.value: One code release with several model presets: monomer (the CASP14 model, no ensembling), monomer_casp14 (num_ensemble=8), monomer_ptm (pTM fine tuned) and multimer (AlphaFold-Multimer). The v2.3.0 technical note describes the current multimer models.

run_guide.summary: Build the Docker image at a pinned commit, download the databases and parameters, and predict the structure of one protein from a FASTA file.
prerequisites: A Linux machine with an NVIDIA GPU, Docker and the NVIDIA Container Toolkit. The README's own note on what was tested: 12 vCPUs, 85 GB of RAM and one A100.
Up to 3 TB of disk for the genetic databases (556 GB to download, 2.62 TB unpacked), or 600 GB with the reduced_dbs preset, which also needs 8 CPU cores and 8 GB of RAM.
aria2c and rsync for the download script.
Code is Apache-2.0; the parameters are CC BY 4.0.

steps.title: Predict one monomer
steps.explanation: The README's monomer example. monomer.fasta holds one sequence; output_dir must be an absolute path. For a complex, use a multi-sequence FASTA and --model_preset=multimer.

quotes.text:
python3 docker/run_docker.py \
  --fasta_paths=monomer.fasta \
  --max_template_date=2021-11-01 \
  --model_preset=monomer \
  --data_dir=$DOWNLOAD_DIR \
  --output_dir=/home/user/absolute_path_to_the_output_dir
set `--model_preset=multimer`,

outputs: A subdirectory of the output directory per target, holding features.pkl, unrelaxed_model_{1..5}.pdb, relaxed PDB files, ranked_{0..4}.pdb, ranking_debug.json, relax_metrics.json, timings.json, result_model_*.pkl and the msas/ directory. ranked_0.pdb is the highest-confidence prediction.
limitations: These commands were read from the repository and have not been executed by Rewire.
The database download is 556 GB and can take a long time; the script is meant to be run in the background.
The run is set up for an NVIDIA GPU; the README offers a CPU option only for the relaxation step (--enable_gpu_relax=false).

notes: The parameter tar files are dated, not versioned by model name, and the current one holds 15 model files (5 CASP14 monomer, 5 pTM, 5 multimer); structured lists the three tar files the README names, with no parameter counts because none is stated and no released dates because the sources give no publication date for them, only the date in the filename. The record describes AlphaFold 2 as released by DeepMind; AlphaFold 3 is a separate model and is not covered. The README is for AlphaFold v2 inference and also documents AlphaFold-Multimer, which may warrant its own record. The README also gives multimer examples for homomers and heteromers and lists the mirrored database licences; those were read.
